tasks.title: control.ts: SpawnAgentInput + per-child slot fields + respawn-on-crash + max-cap + escalation
tasks.description:
Add D12 supervision-strategy plumbing + runtime respawn-on-crash to AgentControl in `packages/opencode/src/agent/control.ts`.

(A) Top-level type aliases (place near the existing exports around L297-323, e.g. directly above `SpawnAgentOptions`):
```ts
export type OnFailureStrategy = "respawn" | "escalate" | "ignore" | "kill_pool"
export type PoolStrategy = "one_for_one" | "one_for_all" | "rest_for_one"
```

(B) Extend `SpawnAgentInput` (around L307-315) with two optional fields:
```ts
readonly on_failure?: OnFailureStrategy
readonly pool_strategy?: PoolStrategy
```
Add a multi-line comment above the new fields explaining D12 (actor-discipline-2026-05-20 Wave 5): defaults must equal current behavior — `on_failure` defaults to `"escalate"` (today's implicit semantics); `pool_strategy` defaults to `"one_for_one"`; the pool field is stub-only here (Wave 6 wires).

(C) Extend `PerRootData` (around L401-433) with four new fields:
```ts
readonly onFailureOf: Map<SessionID, OnFailureStrategy>
readonly poolStrategyOf: Map<SessionID, PoolStrategy>
readonly respawnCountByPath: Map<string, number>
readonly respawnInputByPath: Map<string, SpawnAgentInput>
```
Document each with a comment block referencing D12.

(D) `ensureRootSlot` (around L585-607) MUST initialize the four new maps as empty.

(E) The `Session.Event.Deleted` subscriber teardown (around L522-543) AND the instance-disposal finalizer (around L550-568) MUST clear the four new maps just like the existing per-slot maps. Mirror the existing `slot.skipCompletionNotification.clear()` shape.

(F) `spawnAgent` (around L668-998) MUST store the per-child policy after the child session is created (right alongside the existing `slot.spawnerOf.set(child.id, input.parentPath)` block near L780-797). Defaults: `slot.onFailureOf.set(child.id, input.on_failure ?? "escalate")`, `slot.poolStrategyOf.set(child.id, input.pool_strategy ?? "one_for_one")`. Cache the input on `slot.respawnInputByPath.set(String(childPath), input)`. Initialize `slot.respawnCountByPath` for this path if absent (`if (!slot.respawnCountByPath.has(String(childPath))) slot.respawnCountByPath.set(String(childPath), 0)`).

(G) Respawn logic INSIDE the existing completion-watcher (around L836-951). When the status change handler observes `next` is errored (struct with `errored` key), look up the child's `on_failure` policy:
  - `"respawn"` + `respawnCountByPath < 3`: build a respawn-aware notification with `abort_reason: { reason: "transient_tool_error", details: "respawned after crash; attempt N/3" }` (where N = pre-increment count + 1), send to parent (best-effort, catch send errors), increment `respawnCountByPath` to N, then RELEASE the old child's per-slot state and the registry path:
    ```ts
    slot.mailboxes.delete(child.id)
    slot.statuses.delete(child.id)
    slot.fibers.delete(child.id) // already deleted by onExit but idempotent
    slot.onFailureOf.delete(child.id)
    slot.poolStrategyOf.delete(child.id)
    slot.outgoingToSpawner.delete(child.id)
    slot.spawnerOf.delete(child.id)
    slot.skipCompletionNotification.delete(child.id)
    yield* slot.registry.releaseSpawnedThread(child.id)
    data.sessionToRoot.delete(child.id)
    ```
    Then call `spawnAgent(input)` again with the cached input (the public method itself — re-spawn reuses the path which is now released; PathAlreadyExistsError MUST NOT trigger). Catch any spawn error with `.pipe(Effect.catchAll(() => Effect.void))` to keep the watcher from crashing.
    Then `return yield* Effect.interrupt` to terminate THIS watcher (the new spawn has its own watcher).
  - `"respawn"` + `respawnCountByPath >= 3` (cap exceeded): fall through to the existing notification logic BUT enrich the InterAgentCommunication's `abort_reason` to `{ reason: "transient_tool_error", details: "respawn cap exceeded after 3 attempts" }` (overrides whatever parseAbortReason returned, if any).
  - `"ignore"`: skip the notification entirely (mirror the existing `slot.skipCompletionNotification` flow — set the flag then return-interrupt). The parent sees no completion notification for ignored failures.
  - `"escalate"` (default) and `"kill_pool"`: behave exactly as pre-D12 — existing notification fires unchanged. `kill_pool` is stub-only (stored on slot for Wave 6).

Place the respawn / ignore / cap-override branches BEFORE the existing `header` / `content` / `abortParsed` construction so the existing flow only handles the escalate path. Keep the `isShutdown` skip + the existing safety-net warning logic intact for non-respawn paths.

(H) Export the two new type aliases (`OnFailureStrategy`, `PoolStrategy`) so `agent-spawn.ts` (T2) can import them.

(I) Extend `control.test.ts` with a new top-level `describe("AgentControl D12 supervision strategies", () => { ... })` block placed at the very END of the file (after the existing D11 ABORT block ~L2709 and D9 wasKnownPath block ~L2911). Pattern follows the existing D11 block: reuse the `writeAssistantMessage` helper inline (closure-local). Required tests:
  - `"defaults to escalate when on_failure is not provided (current behavior preserved)"` — spawn without on_failure, child runLoop dies; assert: parent's mailbox has ONE notification with `reached status: errored`, NO `abort_reason: transient_tool_error/respawn` field, child remains errored (no respawn happens — spawnCount via `registerRunLoop` callback assertion).
  - `"on_failure=respawn: child re-spawns at the same task_name with a new session id after a crash"` — runLoop is a closure counter; first invocation `Effect.die("first")`, second writes a normal assistant message + returns. Spawn with on_failure: "respawn"; sleep 100ms; assert: counter === 2; assert: child path resolves to a NEW session id (different from initial spawn's thread_id) via `resolveAgentReference(ROOT, "/root/<name>", root.id)`; assert: parent's mailbox contains a notification with `abort_reason.reason === "transient_tool_error"` AND details matching `/respawned after crash; attempt 1\/3/`.
  - `"on_failure=respawn: max-3 respawns then escalates with respawn-cap-exceeded note"` — runLoop always dies (`Effect.die`). Spawn with on_failure: "respawn"; sleep 200ms; assert: counter === 4 (initial + 3 respawns); assert: parent's mailbox contains the cap-exceeded note (`abort_reason.details` matches `/respawn cap exceeded/` OR contains "3 attempts").
  - `"on_failure=ignore: errored child produces NO completion notification to parent"` — runLoop dies; spawn with on_failure: "ignore"; sleep 100ms; drain parent's mailbox; assert: NO notification from the child's path (drained.find by author returns undefined).
  - `"on_failure=kill_pool: stored but no runtime effect this wave (Wave 6 wires)"` — spawn with on_failure: "kill_pool", verify the spawn succeeds (no schema validation error from AgentControl), child completes normally; assert parent gets the normal completion notification. Stub assertion satisfies the storage requirement.
  - `"pool_strategy stored on the per-child slot (stub for Wave 6)"` — spawn with pool_strategy: "one_for_all"; assert the spawn succeeds without error AND the child receives a normal completion notification (i.e. storage of the policy does not break the spawn flow). No public getter needed in this wave.

Commit message: `wave 5 T1: AgentControl D12 supervision strategies (on_failure + pool_strategy + respawn-on-crash)`.

Gotchas to consult (already loaded by orchestrator): `agentcontrol-providerref-must-live-in-layer-not-instancestate` (single-value layer-scope ref vs InstanceState map — applies to nothing new here; existing per-root slot pattern is correct for the new maps); `agentcontrol-d11-abort-line-parser-last-line-only` (sibling completion-watcher invariant — do not break ABORT parsing); `bun-coverage-aggregation-flake` + `bun-test-coverage-source-file-arg-runs-zero-tests` (single-file test path for coverage). 100% line coverage on src/agent/control.ts via the single-file `bun test --coverage src/agent/control.test.ts` recipe — TaggedErrorClass function% gap is pre-existing per `schema-class-function-coverage` GOTCHA, NOT a regression.

tasks.title: agent-spawn.ts: on_failure + pool_strategy Schema params + tool plumbing
tasks.description:
Extend the `spawn_agent` tool surface in `packages/opencode/src/tool/agent-spawn/agent-spawn.ts` to accept two optional supervision-strategy parameters.

(A) Add two optional fields to the `Parameters` Schema.Struct (around L28-52, AFTER `reasoning_effort`):
```ts
on_failure: Schema.optional(
  Schema.Literal("respawn", "escalate", "ignore", "kill_pool"),
).annotate({
  description:
    "How the runtime supervises this child's terminal failure (D12). `escalate` (default) = today's behavior: forward an errored notification to your mailbox. `respawn` = the runtime re-spawns the child at the same task_name with a fresh session id (capped at 3 attempts, then escalates with a respawn-cap-exceeded notification). `ignore` = swallow the failure silently (no completion notification). `kill_pool` is stub-only in this release; Wave 6 wires pool semantics.",
}),
pool_strategy: Schema.optional(
  Schema.Literal("one_for_one", "one_for_all", "rest_for_one"),
).annotate({
  description:
    "Pool failure semantics (D12, stub-only this release). Stored on the per-child slot for Wave 6 to read when `spawn_pool` lands. `one_for_one` (default) isolates failures; `one_for_all` will tear down the entire pool on any single failure; `rest_for_one` will tear down pool members spawned after the failing one. Today this param has no runtime effect beyond being stored.",
}),
```
The `Schema.Literal(...)` enforces the enum at the model layer; invalid values surface as decode errors before `execute` runs (matches existing fork_turns / agent_type validation discipline).

(B) In the `execute` body (around L132-207), pass the two new params through to `control.spawnAgent`:
```ts
const spawned = yield* control
  .spawnAgent({
    parentID: ctx.sessionID,
    parentPath,
    task_name: params.task_name,
    agent_type: params.agent_type,
    initial_message: params.message,
    options: { fork_turns: fork.value },
    on_failure: params.on_failure,
    pool_strategy: params.pool_strategy,
  })
```
(The T1-extended SpawnAgentInput accepts the optional fields with sensible defaults; undefined cascades through cleanly.)

(C) Add a multi-line comment near the existing PermissionKey block (around L19-27) noting D12 Wave 5 adds supervision-strategy parameters; defaults match today's implicit behavior.

(D) Extend `packages/opencode/src/tool/agent-spawn/agent-spawn.test.ts` with new tests in the existing `describe("tool.spawn_agent", ...)` block (around L95-405):
  - `"on_failure='respawn' passes through (no error)"` — spawn with on_failure: "respawn", assert spawn succeeds, metadata.task_name set, metadata.error undefined.
  - `"on_failure='escalate' passes through (no error)"` — same shape.
  - `"on_failure='ignore' passes through (no error)"` — same shape.
  - `"on_failure='kill_pool' passes through (no error)"` — same shape.
  - `"on_failure='bogus' is rejected by Schema.Literal at decode time"` — try `def.execute({ ..., on_failure: "bogus" as any }, ctx)` (cast for type system) and assert it throws OR returns an error metadata. The exact failure mode depends on whether Schema.optional+Literal is validated at decode (likely yes — test asserts the model-facing surface either rejects or surfaces an error). NOTE: if the Schema validation is enforced at parameter-decode time (not at execute) the test may need to use the registered tool's Parameters schema directly; in that case assert via `Schema.decodeUnknown(Parameters)({ message: 'x', task_name: 'y', agent_type: 'explore', on_failure: 'bogus' })` returns a `Result.Failure`.
  - `"pool_strategy='one_for_all' passes through (no error)"` — spawn with pool_strategy: "one_for_all", assert spawn succeeds.
  - `"pool_strategy='one_for_one' passes through (no error)"` — same shape.
  - `"pool_strategy='rest_for_one' passes through (no error)"` — same shape.
  - `"pool_strategy='invalid' is rejected by Schema.Literal at decode time"` — same shape as the bogus on_failure test.
  - `"on_failure + pool_strategy combined pass through"` — spawn with both set, assert success.
  - `"defaults preserved when neither is provided (existing fork_turns happy path still works)"` — re-run the existing happy-path test shape to confirm no regression.

Commit message: `wave 5 T2: agent-spawn tool accepts on_failure + pool_strategy schema params (D12)`.

100% line coverage on `src/tool/agent-spawn/agent-spawn.ts` via `bun test --coverage src/tool/agent-spawn/agent-spawn.test.ts` recipe. New branches: the Schema.optional fields land transparently; no new code paths in `execute` beyond the spawnAgent call extension.

tasks.title: Tests: INV-D-15..17 integration invariants + agent-spawn.txt prose
tasks.description:
Add INV-D-15..17 integration invariants AND update the `agent-spawn.txt` tool description.

(A) Append THREE new `it.instance` blocks to `packages/opencode/test/integration/multi-agent-invariants.test.ts` inside the existing `describe("INTEGRATION_INVARIANTS — multi-agent surfaces", ...)` block, AFTER the INV-D-14 block (around L1949):

  - `"INV-D-15-spawn-agent-with-on-failure-respawn-restarts-on-crash"`:
    Pattern: same shape as INV-D-13 (closure counter on the runLoop). Register a runLoop that crashes on first invocation (e.g. `Effect.die("first crash")`) and emits a normal completion (assistant message + return "done") on the second. Spawn one child with on_failure: "respawn". Sleep ~150ms. Assert:
    - counter === 2 (initial spawn + 1 respawn)
    - `control.resolveAgentReference(AgentPath.root(), "/root/<task_name>", root.id)` returns a SessionID that is NOT equal to the originally-returned `child.thread_id` (respawned with a fresh session id)
    - parent's mailbox (after drain) contains a notification from the child's path with `abort_reason.reason === "transient_tool_error"` AND `abort_reason.details` matches `/respawned after crash/` AND mentions `/1\/3/`
    - parent's mailbox also contains the SECOND completion notification (normal completion of the respawned child)

  - `"INV-D-16-pool-strategy-one-for-all-kills-pair-on-single-failure"`:
    STUB form per WAVE.md (full pool behavior in Wave 6). Spawn TWO children with pool_strategy: "one_for_all". Assert both spawn succeed (no schema errors). Assert each child's spawn returned a LiveAgent with a valid thread_id. Document via inline comment that full one_for_all behavior (sibling teardown on single failure) lands in Wave 6 when `spawn_pool` is wired; this test pins the param is accepted and the spawn surface is unchanged.

  - `"INV-D-17-pool-strategy-one-for-one-isolates-failures"`:
    STUB form per WAVE.md. Spawn THREE children with pool_strategy: "one_for_one". Make one of them crash via the registered runLoop (counter trick or different runLoop registration). Assert the OTHER two children continue running (status is non-final after sleep ~100ms). Document via inline comment that full one_for_one isolation behavior is the implicit default today; this test pins the param storage does not affect sibling isolation.

(B) Update `packages/opencode/src/tool/agent-spawn/agent-spawn.txt` to document the two new parameters. Insert a new section after `## fork_turns` (end of file, around L112). Section header: `## Supervision strategies (D12)`. Required content:
  - One short paragraph explaining the two parameters are optional and default to today's implicit behavior.
  - Bulleted list of `on_failure` values:
    - `escalate` (default): the runtime forwards an errored notification to your mailbox. You decide what to do next (close, retry, ignore).
    - `respawn`: the runtime re-spawns the child at the same task_name with a fresh session id, capped at 3 attempts. After the cap, the runtime escalates with a respawn-cap-exceeded notification (abort_reason.reason = `transient_tool_error`).
    - `ignore`: the runtime swallows the failure silently. You receive no completion notification. Useful for fire-and-forget probes you do not want to react to.
    - `kill_pool`: stub-only this release. Wave 6 wires pool teardown semantics.
  - Bulleted list of `pool_strategy` values:
    - `one_for_one` (default): pool failures are isolated; surviving siblings keep running.
    - `one_for_all`: any single failure tears down the entire pool. Wired in Wave 6.
    - `rest_for_one`: any single failure tears down pool members spawned after the failing one. Wired in Wave 6.
  - One closing line noting the params are stub-stored on the per-child slot until Wave 6 spawn_pool wires active behavior.

Commit message: `wave 5 T3: INV-D-15..17 integration invariants + supervision-strategies tool description`.

Verification recipe:
- `cd packages/opencode && bun test ./test/integration/multi-agent-invariants.test.ts -t 'INV-D-15-spawn-agent-with-on-failure-respawn-restarts-on-crash'` → 1 pass
- same for INV-D-16, INV-D-17
- `cd packages/opencode && bun test ./test/integration/multi-agent-invariants.test.ts` → all green (was 31 pass; now 34 pass)
- `cd packages/opencode && bun typecheck` → clean
